correctness.rationale: Direct classification of all shortest paths between original and subdivision vertices proves that every monitoring witness for a half-edge contains one of its endpoints, hence MEG implies vertex cover. The converse follows from explicit unique paths; each enumerator is an exact forced/optional-vertex count. Minimality and cardinality extremes follow from explicit indispensable vertices and f(k)-f(k+1)=k-1. Exhaustive independent edge-deletion BFS checks for orders 3..5 and deterministic samples for order 6 agree, while the written proof handles all n>=3.

originality.rationale: A closely related general published theorem already proves vertex-cover sufficiency in this high-girth family; this part is not novel. The identified remaining contribution is necessity for incidence graphs of complete graphs, exact equality of all MEG sets and covers, and exact all-set/minimal-set spectra. These do not follow from prior scalar optimum or subdivision bounds. Search and full-text review did not identify explicit coverage, with provisional priority and listed residual risks.
residual_risks: The reverse MEG=>vertex-cover statement could have been proved independently under incidence-graph or total-subdivision terminology without indexing.
The enumerators are ordinary cover polynomials after the structural equivalence and should not be treated as independently novel algebra.
The structurally adjacent 2025 and product papers were not inspected line-by-line through every appendix.
Approximate semantic literature searches and bibliographic web searches do not prove a global absence of stronger prior theorems.

value.rationale: The underlying probe-placement question is motivated by edge-failure observability. The result is a sharp converse to a known general sufficient vertex-cover condition on a natural infinite incidence-graph family. It classifies the entire monitoring family and all irredundant deployments, obtains exact lower and upper minimal sizes n and binom(n,2)+1, and quantifies unbounded holes in the minimal-set cardinality spectrum. The counting is elementary after the nontrivial structural equivalence, an explicitly acknowledged limitation.
